answer: Price new identities on a rising admission curve. Each epoch the fee for the k-th new account is base x 2^(k/50), paid into the grader pool, and the counter halves every epoch. A lone newcomer pays about base; a farm of 1,000 fakes in one epoch pays over a million times base for the last one, so cost grows exponentially with farm size. Spreading out only slows a farm to a whisper of fifty per epoch, never an ocean, and honest arrivals caught in a surge get the excess refunded once a graded answer settles, so they can still root like cedar.
